---
title: "Models"
---

`lm()`, `glm()`, `lmer()`, and `glmer()` pass the input table to the phit
extension's `Phit\fit_lm()`, `Phit\fit_glm()`, `Phit\fit_lmer()`, and `Phit\fit_glmer()`. The extension reads factor levels from the
table, builds the model matrix, and returns coefficients, standard errors, and
fit statistics in the same order as R.

::: {.panel-tabset group="syntax"}

## Method chain (PHP 8.3+)

```php
phplyr($table)->lm('y ~ x + group');
phplyr($table)->glm('passed ~ hours', family: 'binomial');   // also 'poisson', link:
phplyr($table)->lmer('score ~ hours + (1 | school)');        // REML; reml: false for ML
phplyr($table)->glmer('passed ~ hours + (1 | school)', family: 'binomial');
```

## Pipe (PHP 8.5)

```php
$table |> lm('y ~ x + group');
$table |> glm('passed ~ hours', family: 'binomial');   // also 'poisson', link:
$table |> lmer('score ~ hours + (1 | school)');        // REML; reml: false for ML
$table |> glmer('passed ~ hours + (1 | school)', family: 'binomial');
```

:::

`lmer()` and `glmer()` take lme4's random-effect bars. The result includes
`columns` with R's coefficient names. All four need phit with the formula
functions. Without the extension they
throw an exception that says so.
